faq.q: How much does Gomez Trial Attorneys charge?
faq.a: Gomez Trial Attorneys publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does Gomez Trial Attorneys offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Gomez Trial Attorneys publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock, the firm states it will visit clients in hospital or at home and it publishes material in Spanish.

faq.q: Where does Gomez Trial Attorneys have offices?
faq.a: Gomez Trial Attorneys publishes five offices, in San Diego, Solana Beach, Riverside, Temecula and El Centro. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at Gomez Trial Attorneys?
faq.a: Gomez Trial Attorneys names 50 attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: California does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.q: Are the case results Gomez Trial Attorneys publishes verified?
faq.a: No. Gomez Trial Attorneys publishes 20 case results with amounts on its own site. We counted them and we did not confirm them: the figures are the firm's. Pillar B scores whether a firm publishes outcomes and discloses them properly, including whether a prior-results disclaimer appears beside them, not whether the amounts are right. Past results do not predict another case.
